title: Government & Post Office Schemes
intro: Government-backed savings, post office deposits and retirement schemes; compare the rate, how long your money is locked in, tax treatment and whether the government guarantees it.
newsQuery: small savings schemes interest rate India
sources: Ministry of Finance (DEA) Office Memorandum F. No.1/4/2019-NS dated 30 Sep 2026: small savings rates for 1 Oct-31 Dec 2026 (unchanged)
Department of Posts SB Order No. 12/2026; indiapost.gov.in / nsiindia.gov.in scheme rules
EPFO 239th CBT meeting, 2 Mar 2026 (PIB): EPF rate 8.25% for FY 2025-26
NPS Tier I scheme returns as of 18 Sep 2026 (SBI Pension Funds, via hdfcsec.com NPS returns page)
PFRDA / NPS Trust scheme rules for NPS and Atal Pension Yojana

params.label: Interest rate / return
params.tip: Rate for Oct-Dec 2026 quarter (MoF notification, 30 Sep 2026). NPS: 5-year Tier I return of SBI Pension Funds as of 18 Sep 2026, market-linked, not a fixed rate. EPF: FY 2025-26 declared rate.

params.label: Compounding / payout
params.tip: How interest is compounded or paid out, per scheme rules.

params.label: Lock-in / tenure
params.tip: Maturity period in years per scheme rules (Oct 2026). Blank where money is locked until age 60 or retirement.

params.label: Minimum investment
params.tip: Minimum deposit per scheme rules (Oct 2026); RD is per month, PPF/SSY/NPS per year.

params.label: Maximum investment
params.tip: Deposit cap per scheme rules (Oct 2026); blank means no upper limit or not a fixed rupee cap.

params.label: Tax deduction (80C/80CCD)
params.tip: Deposit qualifies for deduction under 80C (or 80CCD for NPS/APY). Only available under the old tax regime. Rules as of Oct 2026.

params.label: Interest taxable
params.tip: Whether interest/returns are taxed at your slab rate (Oct 2026 rules).

params.label: Government guarantee
params.tip: Backed by the Government of India (Oct 2026).

items.name: Public Provident Fund (PPF)

v.eligibility: Resident Indian individuals; one account per person (minors via guardian)
v.liquidity: Partial withdrawal from year 7; loan in years 3-6; extendable in 5-year blocks

cons: Rate unchanged at 7.1% for many quarters, can be cut
items.best: Long-term tax-free saving for anyone in the old tax regime

items.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana

v.eligibility: Parent/guardian of a girl child below 10 years; max two girls per family
v.liquidity: 50% withdrawal after girl turns 18 for education; closure for marriage after 18

cons: Only for a girl child under 10
items.best: Parents saving for a daughter's education or marriage

items.name: National Savings Certificate (NSC VIII)

v.eligibility: Resident Indian individuals, including joint and minor accounts
v.liquidity: No premature exit except death or court order; can be pledged as loan security

pros: Rate locked for 5 years at purchase
items.best: Old-regime taxpayers wanting a fixed 5-year rate with 80C benefit

items.name: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP)

v.compounding: Compounded yearly; amount doubles in 115 months
v.eligibility: Resident Indian adults, joint holders, guardians for minors

pros: Money doubles in 115 months (9 yr 7 mo)
items.best: Conservative savers who want a known doubling period

items.name: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS)

v.eligibility: Age 60+; 55-60 for retired civilians and 50+ for retired defence (within rules)
v.liquidity: Premature closure allowed with penalty (1.5% before 2 yrs, 1% after); extendable by 3 years

items.best: Retirees needing regular, safe quarterly income
items.news: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme interest rate

items.name: Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS)

v.eligibility: Resident Indian adults; joint up to 3; Rs 15 lakh cap for joint accounts
v.liquidity: Closure after 1 year: 2% deduction before 3 yrs, 1% after

pros: Rs 15 lakh cap in joint account
items.best: Anyone wanting a fixed monthly income from a lump sum

items.name: Post Office Time Deposit - 1 year

v.eligibility: Resident Indian adults, joint, minors via guardian
v.liquidity: No withdrawal for 6 months; before 1 year earns savings rate

cons: Early exit earns only savings rate
items.best: Parking money safely for about a year
items.news: Post Office time deposit interest rate

items.name: Post Office Time Deposit - 2 years

v.eligibility: Resident Indian adults, joint, minors via guardian
v.liquidity: Exit after 6 months; after 1 year, rate is 2% less than the deposit rate

items.best: Two-year goals needing a guaranteed return
items.news: Post Office time deposit interest rate

items.name: Post Office Time Deposit - 3 years

v.eligibility: Resident Indian adults, joint, minors via guardian
v.liquidity: Exit after 6 months; after 1 year, rate is 2% less than the deposit rate

items.best: Medium-term savers comparing against bank FDs
items.news: Post Office time deposit interest rate

items.name: Post Office Time Deposit - 5 years

v.eligibility: Resident Indian adults, joint, minors via guardian
v.liquidity: Exit after 6 months; after 1 year, rate is 2% less than the deposit rate

items.best: Tax-saving FD alternative for conservative investors

items.name: Post Office Recurring Deposit (5-year)

v.eligibility: Resident Indian adults, joint, minors via guardian
v.liquidity: Loan up to 50% after 12 instalments; premature closure after 3 years at savings rate

items.best: Small monthly savers wanting a disciplined, safe plan
items.news: Post Office recurring deposit interest rate

items.name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)

v.compounding: Guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000-5,000 from age 60
v.eligibility: Indian citizens aged 18-40 with a bank/post office account; not income-tax payers (from Oct 2022)
v.liquidity: Locked till 60; voluntary exit returns only own contributions plus actual earnings

pros: Pension passes to spouse, then corpus to nominee
cons: Pension fixed in rupees, eroded by inflation
Contribution depends on age at joining

items.name: NPS Tier I - Equity (Scheme E)

v.liquidity: Locked till 60; partial withdrawals for specific needs after 3 years

pros: Equity growth with very low fund costs
Extra Rs 50,000 deduction under 80CCD(1B) in the old regime
cons: Returns not guaranteed; 1-year return was negative (-4.13%) as of Sep 2026
Part of corpus must buy an annuity at exit
items.best: Long-horizon retirement savers comfortable with market risk

items.name: NPS Tier I - Corporate Bonds (Scheme C)

v.liquidity: Locked till 60; partial withdrawals for specific needs after 3 years

cons: Not guaranteed; credit and rate risk
items.best: Debt part of an NPS allocation

items.name: NPS Tier I - Government Securities (Scheme G)

v.liquidity: Locked till 60; partial withdrawals for specific needs after 3 years

pros: No credit risk on underlying bonds
items.best: Low-credit-risk debt part of an NPS allocation

items.name: EPF / Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF)

v.compounding: Interest on monthly running balance, credited yearly
v.eligibility: Salaried employees of EPF-covered establishments; VPF is extra voluntary contribution
v.liquidity: Partial withdrawals for housing, education, medical etc.; full on retirement or after 2 months unemployed

pros: 8.25% for FY 2025-26, above most small savings
cons: Interest on employee contribution above Rs 2.5 lakh/yr is taxable
Rate declared yearly by EPFO, not a sovereign guarantee
items.best: Salaried people wanting high safe debt returns via VPF
